tools._comment_ffmpeg: Topaz's ffmpeg has no libx264/libx265 (no --enable-gpl in its build) -- only hardware encoders (h264_nvenc/hevc_nvenc/amf/qsv/mf). We use h264_nvenc throughout for both the deinterlace-stage mezzanine and the Topaz upscale output, since the RTX 3090 makes this fast and good quality. ffmpeg_libx264 below is a full GPL ffmpeg build (has libx264/libx265) kept as an optional swap-in if you ever want exact software-encode parity with the guide.

_comment_tvai_model_dir: Topaz's ffmpeg.exe normally inherits this from Topaz Video.exe when it launches ffmpeg itself; run standalone, tvai_up fails with 'Model not found' unless we set it explicitly.
_comment_neuroserver: neuroserver.exe (Topaz's separate local diffusion-model service, used for generative Starlight models -- these are NOT reachable through ffmpeg's tvai_up filter at all) needs TOPAZ_MODEL_STORE set explicitly when run standalone, same reasoning as tvai_model_dir above. On this machine the actual weight store was relocated to the Z: drive (not the default C:\ProgramData location) -- confirmed by a Process Monitor capture of a real Topaz Video AI GUI render. neuroserver's OWN internal post-process step (a second tvai_up pass) also shells out to a bare 'ffmpeg' on PATH rather than using its own bundled one, so PATH must have Topaz's ffmpeg directory prepended before launching it or that internal step fails with 'Filter not found' (using system PATH found the GPL ffmpeg from winget instead, which lacks --enable-tvai).
_comment_vs_plugins: DLL paths reused from the Hybrid install (Hybrid\64bit\vsfilters\...) so our own .vpy scripts drive the exact same QTGMC/VIVTC engine Hybrid's GUI uses, without a second VapourSynth setup. Loaded defensively (missing/optional ones are skipped) -- see vpy_templates/_plugins.vpy.j2.
_comment_checkpoint: Generative (Starlight) upscales can take days -- upscale.py's _run_generative splits the source into segments at black-frame boundaries (found once via ffmpeg's blackdetect filter) so a crash/pause/VRAM-fragmentation stop only loses at most one segment's worth of work, not the whole job. Segment outputs are copied here (NOT the R:\ staging RAM disk, which is wiped on reboot) so they survive a restart.
